title_en: Xingtian Dances with Axe and Shield
full_text_zh:
[P1] 给孩子的山海经神话绘本
刑天舞干戚
孟惜 编 〔西〕徐丽娅·文森特 绘
北京科学技术出版社
中国国家博物馆 文化创意产品授权出版

[P2] 给孩子的山海经神话绘本
刑天舞干戚
孟惜 编 〔西〕徐丽娅·文森特 绘

国家开放大学出版社出版 〔京开童媒（北京）文化传媒有限公司出品
北京

[P3] 在涿鹿之战中，黄帝打败并擒了炎帝的手下蚩尤。蚩尤有一个朋友，也是炎帝的大臣，名叫刑天。他怒气冲冲地要去找黄帝报仇，于是请求炎帝举兵对抗黄帝，可是炎帝早已没有了斗志，只求平安，因此拒绝出兵。

[P4] 愤怒的刑天独自出发了，只身一人去向黄帝挑战。他左手握着一面坚固的盾牌，右手挥舞着一柄巨大的斧头。一路过关斩将，砍开重重天门，杀到黄帝的宫门外。

[P5] 闻此消息，黄帝拿起宝剑，亲自迎战。两人一个用剑刺，一个用斧劈，从宫内打到宫外，从天庭打到凡间，直到一个叫做常羊山的地方。

[P6] 一个是骁勇善战的黄帝，一个是高大魁梧的巨人刑天，他们争斗得异常激烈。战斗经验丰富的黄帝抓住机会，一剑向刑天劈去。只听“咔嚓”一声，刑天的巨大头颅被砍了下来。

[P7] 刑天一摸脖子上没有了头颅，顿时惊慌起来，伸出手在地上乱摸乱抓。他要寻找到那颗不屈的头颅，安在脖颈上，再和黄帝大战一场。

[P8] 他摸呀摸呀，周围的大小山谷被他摸了个遍。
参天的大树、突出的岩石……在他的触摸下，都折断了，崩塌了，可还是没有找到那颗头颅。他只顾向远处摸去，却没想到头颅就在离他不远的山脚下。

[P9] 黄帝不想让刑天找到头颅，他很快举起宝剑，向常羊山纵身劈去。一阵天崩地裂的轰隆声瞬间响彻四方，高耸的常羊山被砍成了两半，刑天的头颅滚到了中间的裂缝中。

[P10] 紧接着，两山合二为一，把刑天的头颅深深地埋葬了。
听到异动声的刑天意识到，自己的头颅恐怕再也找不回来了。他呆呆地跪在那里，就像是一座沉沉的大山。

[P11] 刑天不甘心就这样败在黄帝手下。
他突然站起身，一只手拿着盾牌，一只手举起大斧，向着天空乱劈乱舞，继续
和看不见的敌人拼死搏斗起来。

[P12] 失去头的刑天，赤裸着他的上身，把两乳当作眼睛，把肚脐当作嘴巴，他的身躯就是头颅。那两眼似乎在喷射出愤怒的火焰，那张开的嘴巴似乎在发出仇恨的咒骂，那被当作头颅的身躯如山一样坚实稳固，那两手拿着的斧和盾，挥舞得是那样的有力。

[P13] 看着无头刑天还在愤怒地挥舞盾斧，黄帝心里一阵颤栗，也有一丝敬畏，他不再对刑天下手，而是悄悄地回天宫去了。

[P14] 乱舞了一阵的刑天耗尽气力，岿然倒下。
但他仍然像一座高耸的山一样。

[P15] 后来，东晋诗人陶渊明被刑天的精神感动，
写下诗句：“刑天舞干戚，猛志固常在。”干就是盾牌，戚是指斧子。以此赞美刑天这位英雄
顽强不屈的精神。
full_text_en:
[P1] Mythological Picture Book of the Classic of Mountains and Seas for Children
Xingtian Dances with Shield and Axe
Compiled by Meng Xi, Illustrated by [Spain] Mireia Vincent
Beijing Science and Technology Press
Authorized Creative Product Publication by the National Museum of China

[P2] A Mythology Picture Book from the Classic Shan Hai Jing for Children
Xingtian Dances with His Weapons
Compiled by Meng Xi, Illustrated by [Spain] Xuliya Wenxintei

Published by Open University of China Press, Produced by Jingkai Children's Media (Beijing) Cultural Communication Co., Ltd.
Beijing

[P3] In the Battle of Zhuolu, the Yellow Emperor defeated and captured Chiyou, a subordinate of the Flame Emperor. Chiyou had a friend, who was also a minister of the Flame Emperor, named Xingtian. Filled with rage, he wanted to seek revenge against the Yellow Emperor and thus requested the Flame Emperor to raise troops to fight back. However, the Flame Emperor had already lost his fighting spirit and only sought peace, so he refused to send out the army.

[P4] Furious,刑天 set out alone to challenge the Yellow Emperor. He held a sturdy shield in his left hand and swung a massive axe in his right. He fought his way through, cutting through重重 heavenly gates, and reached the gates of the Yellow Emperor's palace.

[P5] Upon hearing this news, the Yellow Emperor picked up his sacred sword and fought in person. One used a sword to stab, the other used an axe to chop. They fought from inside the palace to outside, from the heavenly realm to the mortal world, until they reached a place called Changyang Mountain.

[P6] One was the brave and valiant Emperor Huang, the other was the tall and mighty giant Xingtian. They fought fiercely. The battle-experienced Emperor Huang seized the opportunity and slashed at Xingtian with his sword. With a 'crack' sound, Xingtian's huge head was severed.

[P7] Craving Tian touched his neck and found his head was gone. He became instantly panicked, reaching out and frantically searching the ground. He wanted to find his indomitable head, place it back on his neck, and fight Emperor Huang again.

[P8] He touched and touched, searching every big and small valley around him.
Towering trees, jutting rocks... under his touch, they all broke and collapsed, yet he still couldn't find his head. He kept reaching out toward the distance, not realizing his head was at the foot of the mountain not far away.

[P9] Huangdi didn't want Xingtian to find his head, so he quickly raised his sword and slashed toward Mount Changyang. A thunderous crash echoed through the skies, splitting the towering Mount Changyang in two. Xingtian's head rolled into the crack in the middle.

[P10] Next, the two mountains merged into one, deeply burying刑天's head.
Hearing the commotion,刑天 realized his head was probably lost forever. He knelt there, motionless, like a heavy, towering mountain.

[P11] Xingtian was unwilling to accept defeat at the hands of the Yellow Emperor.
He suddenly stood up, holding a shield in one hand and raising a great axe in the other, wildly slashing and dancing toward the sky, continuing to fight desperately against the invisible enemy.

[P12] The headless Jing Tian, bare-chested, used his two nipples as eyes and his navel as a mouth; his body became his head. Those eyes seemed to spew flames of rage, and that open mouth seemed to utter curses of hatred. The body serving as his head was as solid and steady as a mountain, while his two hands, wielding axe and shield, swung with such powerful force.

[P13] Seeing the headless Jing Tian still angrily swinging his shield and axe, the Yellow Emperor felt a shiver in his heart, along with a touch of awe. He no longer attacked Jing Tian, but quietly returned to the Heavenly Palace.

[P14] After wildly dancing for a while,刑天 exhausted his strength and fell, yet he remained as steadfast as a towering mountain.

[P15] Later, the Eastern Jin poet Tao Yuanming was moved by the spirit of Jing Tian,
and wrote the lines: 'Jing Tian dances with shield and axe, his fierce will remains forever.' 'Gan' refers to a shield, and 'Qi' refers to an axe. With this, he praised Jing Tian's heroic
spirit of unyielding perseverance.
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《刑天舞干戚》的封面，展示了主角刑天手持武器、英勇威武的形象，背景为山川河流，上方标明书名、编绘者及出版社信息。
[P2] 本页为绘本《刑天舞干戚》的扉页，展示了书名、编绘者信息及出版社信息，配有一座立于云朵之上的中式楼阁插图。
[P3] 本页讲述了涿鹿之战后，蚩尤被黄帝击败，其好友刑天欲为他报仇，请求炎帝出兵对抗黄帝，但炎帝因无斗志而拒绝出兵。
[P4] 刑天因蚩尤被黄帝击败而愤怒，独自一人手持盾牌和斧头，一路斩将夺关，杀到黄帝宫门外。
[P5] 黄帝得知刑天来袭后亲自出战，与刑天展开激烈战斗，从宫殿打到凡间，最终战斗延伸至常羊山。
[P6] 黄帝与刑天在常羊山展开激烈战斗，黄帝抓住机会一剑砍下刑天的头颅。
[P7] 刑天被黄帝斩下头颅后，惊慌地在地上寻找自己的头颅，希望能重新安上，再与黄帝一战。黄帝在一旁冷眼旁观。
[P8] 刑天在失去头颅后，焦急地在山谷中四处摸索寻找自己的头，却始终未能找到，而头颅其实就在他不远处的山脚下。
[P9] 黄帝为防止刑天找回头颅，挥剑劈开常羊山，将刑天的头颅埋入山体裂缝中。
[P10] 黄帝将刑天的头颅埋入山中，刑天在失去头颅后呆立原地，如同一座沉沉的大山。
[P11] 刑天在被黄帝斩下头颅后，仍不甘心失败，以无头之躯手持盾牌和大斧，继续向天空挥舞，与看不见的敌人搏斗。
[P12] 刑天在被黄帝斩下头颅后，以无头之躯继续战斗，将两乳当作眼睛、肚脐当作嘴巴，手持斧盾，如山般稳固地挥舞，表现出不屈的战斗意志。
[P13] 黄帝目睹无头的刑天仍在愤怒地挥舞武器，心生敬畏，遂放弃继续攻击，悄然返回天宫。
[P14] 刑天在耗尽力气后倒下，但其身躯依然如山般屹立，象征着不屈的意志。
[P15] 本页描绘东晋诗人陶渊明在烛光下书写诗句，赞颂刑天虽被斩首却仍挥舞斧盾、不屈战斗的精神，画面右侧以云雾中刑天的无头形象呼应其顽强意志。
[P16] 本页画面描绘东晋诗人陶渊明在烛光下书写诗句，赞颂刑天虽被斩首却仍挥舞斧盾、不屈战斗的精神，画面右侧以云雾中刑天的无头形象呼应其顽强意志。
